bounds: A SAFE, or Simple Agreement for Future Equity, is a contract that may give an investor equity later if a specified event occurs.
It is not the same as owning common stock today, and it is generally not a loan that promises repayment with interest.
Some convert during a qualifying equity financing; others describe what happens during a sale or shutdown.
A trigger may never occur, so a SAFE may never convert.
Even if it converts, the number and class of shares depend on the contract and later capitalization.
Read the triggering events, valuation cap, discount, conversion mechanics, and any treatment in a sale or dissolution.
Do not translate a cap into a guaranteed ownership percentage.
A SAFE can be simple in name but still have important legal and economic details.
Compare it with other outstanding SAFEs and future financing plans, and get qualified advice if the language is unclear.
